q: he’s never been a great sleeper but before he would sleep after I nursed him but now he’s still crying or whimpering and jerking himself awake.
x: Breastfeeding mother of a 10-month-old waking several times a night for weeks.

q: I have the baby all day while dad is at work (except I return to work in 2 weeks), when dad gets home he takes over so I can sleep, and I take back over midnight so dad can sleep for work. This just isn’t sustainable what so ever.
x: Mother of a 10-week-old who stopped sleeping in the cot at nine weeks.

q: I don’t mind the contact napping during the day because I am AWAKE AND ALERT and love the cuddles
x: Same mother on what she does not want changed.

q: The 3-8pm stretch is atrocious and I don’t know how to fix it.
x: Same mother after logging her baby's full day hour by hour.

q: He goes to daycare and is on one nap (two isn't possible there so we had to transition early).
x: Parent of a 14-month-old with three months of split nights.

q: Sometimes, he sleeps 2+ hours and their policy is to not wake a kid up if they're sleeping long
x: Same parent on the daycare nap.

q: This leads me to believe that he is now overtired. Now I don't know what else to do. I've been considering wakig him up even earlier so he has a longer first WW and then a shorter second one but the information out there is so contradicting
x: Same parent after stretching wake windows for suspected undertiredness.

q: The weird thing is that about every 3 nights, we get a "perfect" night where he will just sleep for 11-12 hours straight, followed by then again some rougher nights.
x: Same parent.

q: After about 5 nights, it started getting better and now we have had 4 very good nights (trying to keep his WW at at least 5.5 or longer per WW).
x: Same parent five days later, crediting a walking milestone rather than the schedule.

q: I have a 6 week old (I'm not sleep training yet don't worry just hear me out) who has always been a pretty good sleeper.
x: Mother of a 6-week-old heads off criticism before asking.

q: I just don't know what I'm doing and don't want to ruin my good sleeper and make things harder for her later because I know sleep is so important.
x: Same mother on preventing bad habits.

q: My patience is at an all time low and I am starting to feel frustrated with her which is then making me feel guilty.
x: First-time mother of a 5.5-month-old who wakes often and naps only on her.

q: I always wanted two babies and now I’m not sure as I feel I can’t even cope with just one… so deflated I could just cry.
x: Same mother.

q: Fix schedule before CIO or can we do both simultaneously?
x: Parents of a 6-month-old (5 months corrected) planning crying-based training, among four numbered questions.

q: My son was always an okay sleeper and then took to CIO sleep training so easily at 5 months but this girl is so so different than my first. I’m losing my mind from the sleep deprivation so i am counting down to sleep traninf, but also terrified that it won’t work on her.
x: Parent of an almost 12-week-old 'high needs' second baby.

q: she is coming up on 12 weeks and i’ve read you can start sleep training at 14 weeks so i’m trying to prepare.
x: Same parent on the date they are counting down to.

q: He’s the light of my life and he also tortures me. He’s refuses all naps unless it’s on me and he nurses to sleep.
x: Mother of an almost 5-month-old who cries if she walks away.

q: Idk what to do and I feel guilty for being over this. I love a cuddle with him but I’m desperate to be able to do what will make me feel human.
x: Same mother.

q: My question is: should I be starting his first wake window after he’s fully awake and done feeding, or still from the 7am wake-up no matter what?
x: Parent of an almost 6-month-old, 'overthinking' the start of the first wake window.

q: So you can imagine how it goes if we simply try to change his nappy, give him a sip of water and put him back down instead of giving him his feed - he simply won't have it, and then he's worked up and refuses to sleep even if we do give him the feed
x: Parent of a 14-month-old who still takes a full bottle at night.
